title: Provider, process-lock and workspace inventory adapters
description:
Objective: land the production enumerators for the provider/process/launch-lock class and the workspace class, registered into the recovery-inventory port registry. Slice 2 of 3 from task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a, split by architect-d46fcb95 on human direction 2026-08-09.

Hard dependency: task-00956ac383784e81b0345bbf09256323 (Recovery-inventory contract and coverage protocol) must land first - it owns the class set, the item shape, the coverage proof, the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer and the port registry this slice plugs into. Do not restate or re-derive any of them here.

MEASURED PRESENT at 2026-08-09 by architect-d46fcb95 - every primitive this slice calls already exists, so nothing here needs a prerequisite:
- provider capability probes: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-probe.ts (probeClaudeRuntime, capabilityStatus) and providers/codex/codex-probe.ts (probeCodexRuntime, capabilityStatus).
- launch-lock records: packages/runner/src/supervisor/launch-lock.ts (LaunchLockRegistration, parseLaunchLockRegistration, registerLaunchLock, bindsClaim). NOTE: this module is deliberately NOT root-exported; import it relatively from inside the package, do not publish it.
- process observation: packages/runner/src/supervisor/process-observation.ts (BoundProcessObservation, intakeProcessObservation). Its own comment is the rule this slice must honour - "UNOBSERVED is not death. Only an observed exit or signal proves an end."
- workspace manifests: packages/runner/src/workspace/workspace-manifest.ts (buildInputManifest, buildResultManifest) and workspace-contract.ts (WorkspaceInputManifest, WorkspaceInputEntry, WorkspaceTreeEntry).

Deliverable: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/provider-lock-inventory.ts (+ .js bridge) and workspace-inventory.ts (+ .js bridge) plus focused tests, each registering itself as a class enumerator through the contract slice's port registry.

NOT in scope: the contract, coverage protocol or aggregate (slice 1); Git refs, integration targets or artifact objects (slice 3); scheduler resource rows; adopt/quarantine decisions; project embargo; tests/fault.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/provider-lock-inventory.{ts,js}, workspace-inventory.{ts,js}, their focused tests, and the two-line registration edit in the slice-1 aggregate. This slice does NOT edit index.ts or index-surface.test.ts - slice 1 owns the root seam.

Consumer (global rail Clause 1): daemon coordinator task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test
definitionOfDone: The provider/process/launch-lock enumerator calls the shipped probeClaudeRuntime/probeCodexRuntime capability surfaces and the launch-lock and process-observation records, binding every item to its class, stable external identity, observed disposition facts and source proof digest; it never treats a quiet process or an empty probe result as absence.

The workspace enumerator reads real workspace input/result manifests through the shipped workspace-manifest surface and binds each workspace item the same way, refusing rather than merging when two entries claim one external identity.

An unavailable enumerator, an unsupported or absent provider capability, a truncated or over-limit result, and a missing negative proof each return RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN at layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER with truth UNKNOWN; partial items never upgrade the class to COMPLETE.

Both enumerators are registered with the slice-1 port registry and a test proves the aggregate reports COMPLETE for these two classes only when the enumerator actually proved completeness, and UNKNOWN in every other case including the absent-registration case.

Focused tests exercise real temporary filesystem bytes and the shipped provider-probe surfaces rather than a reimplemented fixture authority, assert each covered class generated at least one coverage case with a non-zero asserted count, pin the exact code and INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer on every refusal, and mutation-check that the coverage handling is reddenable.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0, with any residual red attributed to foreign paths against a recorded merge-base baseline.
taskRails: A configured class requires complete enumeration or a verifiable negative proof; an empty list, a quiet process, an absent optional probe, or a mock response is never COMPLETE by itself.

Reuse the shipped probes, launch-lock records, process observation and workspace manifests. Do not reimplement any of their authority inside this module or inside a test helper; a property must be asserted against the production surface.
supervisor/launch-lock.ts is intentionally unpublished. Import it relatively within the package and do not add it to the @moe/runner root seam.
Tests assert the exact stable reason code and the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer, and assert non-zero generated class coverage.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file, not per task.

SEAM UNDERSTOOD (read-only). Read contract:157/171, shape:202 readPortResult, aggregate:68 collectRecoveryInventory and :206 collectClass end to end. Confirmed the plan's account and pinned the precedence order I must design against, since it decides WHICH reason a case can reach:

collectClass order (recovery-inventory.ts:211-245): unregistered -> throw(ENUMERATOR_FAILED) -> unreadable(RESULT_MALFORMED) -> UNAVAILABLE -> UNSUPPORTED -> items.length > 4096 (RESULT_OVER_LIMIT) -> !complete (RESULT_TRUNCATED) -> admitItems. admitItems (:254) then runs shape/class/project/window/duplicate per item, and ONLY at :290 checks "empty AND negativeProofDigest === null -> NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING".

Three consequences that shape both enumerators:
1. NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING is reachable only with complete:true and zero items. So "cannot prove I saw everything" must be expressed as complete:false (RESULT_TRUNCATED), and "saw nothing, cannot prove nothing exists" as complete:true + null digest. Those are different facts and I will not collapse them.
2. readPortResult reads items through readList(value, MAX+1) (shape:213), so a population above 4097 reads as RESULT_MALFORMED rather than RESULT_OVER_LIMIT. Both are UNKNOWN and neither is COMPLETE, so the seam never admits an over-large population; the OVER_LIMIT case must be driven with exactly 4097 items.
3. The enumerator mints NO code. Every DoD 3 case is therefore asserted end to end through collectRecoveryInventory. Where I additionally assert an enumerator's own reading (the unobserved-process disposition facts), that is still the production surface - the exported enumerator itself - not a reimplementation of the aggregate's mapping.

Vocabularies confirmed frozen and sufficient; I invent nothing. Shape helpers to consume: identityKey (:121), readInventoryItem (:164). Ceilings 4096/400/32 confirmed. Also measured for design: MAX_WORKSPACE_ENTRIES is 4096 (workspace-contract.ts:9), and readIdentity (:106) normalizes backslashes in PATH identities but preserves OPAQUE bytes - that normalization is what makes the workspace duplicate case real.

Cases, each pinning truth+code+reason+layer together by whole-object equality (never "it refused"):
- happy path: 1 lock + 1 observed process -> COMPLETE, 2 items, class/projectTag/observedAt bound, sourceProofDigest matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, exact facts asserted for both rows.
- the one-time bootstrap credential digest never appears anywhere in the emitted items.
- a lock binding a foreign wrapper is reported with bindsGoverningClaim:false, not dropped.

- ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED with the class still present in the report.

implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. provider-lock-inventory.ts (248 physical lines by grep -c '') plus the one-line .js bridge; focused run 20/20 pass.

Composes only shipped authority: probeClaudeRuntime/probeCodexRuntime with capabilityStatus imported ALIASED (claudeCapabilityStatus / codexCapabilityStatus - the collision the plan warned about is real and unaliased imports do not compile), parseLaunchLockRegistration + bindsClaim for lock records, intakeProcessObservation for process disposition, parseEffectClaim for the governing claim. launch-lock.ts is imported RELATIVELY and stays unpublished; index.ts and index-surface.test.ts are untouched.

ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE STEP TEXT, and it follows the step-1 ruling rather than contradicting it. The step says "export a RecoveryInventoryRegistration CONSTANT". A constant cannot carry per-composition ports without module-global state, which is precisely the order-dependent coupling createRecoveryInventoryRegistry refused. So the module exports providerLockInventoryRegistration(input): RecoveryInventoryRegistration - a factory returning a frozen { class, enumerate } tuple member. The daemon composes the real one; tests compose their own. Zero aggregate edits, and slice 3 can land the same shape without colliding.

DESIGN DECISION WORTH QA'S ATTENTION: a provider is NOT emitted as a recoverable row. The two probes are the authority that says (a) whether this population can be observed at all - gated on PROCESS_TREE_TERMINATION through the real capabilityStatus, UNSUPPORTED -> CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED - and (b) whether its absence can be proven - RUN_ENUMERATION_NEGATIVE_PROOF on BOTH providers mints negativeProofDigest, otherwise null. Emitting a row per provider would make the class permanently non-empty and silently retire the negative-proof requirement the empty case exists to enforce. Rows are launch locks and process observations only.

Fail-closed mapping, chosen against the aggregate's precedence order measured in step 2:
- probe refuses (bad clock/platform), port throws, or claim unparsable -> UNAVAILABLE, never an empty ENUMERATED.
- process tree unobservable on either provider -> UNSUPPORTED.
- a record this seam cannot read (lock or process) -> complete:false, so an unreadable record truncates the enumeration instead of shrinking the population.
- an UNOBSERVED process -> row KEPT with exitKind UNOBSERVED, dispositionProven false, ended FALSE, and complete:false. Never omitted, never terminated. `ended` is computed from processExit.kind !== "UNOBSERVED" so the drill target is a single explicit expression.
- empty population -> complete:true with negativeProofDigest null when unprovable, which is the only shape that reaches NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING.
The bootstrap credential digest is excluded from facts (launch-lock keeps it out of every outcome) but stays inside the one-way sourceProofDigest, and a test asserts it never appears in the emitted items.

.js bridge verified with od -c: `export * from "./provider-lock-inventory.ts";\n`, trailing LF present, byte-identical in form to the three sibling slice-1 bridges.

implementationPlan.note:
RED THEN GREEN, and this time the red was observed and recorded. I wrote workspace-inventory.test.ts first, then landed a STUB whose enumerator returned UNAVAILABLE unconditionally, and ran it: "Tests 9 failed | 4 passed (13)" with the failures naming the right assertions - two arms expecting COMPLETE got UNKNOWN, the duplicate arm died on "expected an enumeration, got UNAVAILABLE", and the four reason-specific arms failed comparing UNKNOWN reasons. Only the three genuinely-UNAVAILABLE arms passed, which is exactly the shape a correct stub should leave. Then I replaced the stub with the real enumerator: 13/13 green, and the whole recovery-inventory directory is 89/89 across 3 files.

REAL BYTES, NOT A DOUBLE: every workspace is an mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-recovery-ws-")) directory OUTSIDE the repo, with files actually written; afterEach removes it with rmSync recursive+force so it runs on failure too. The production enumerator does the walk itself (readdir recursive + readFile + sha256Hex) and seals through the shipped buildInputManifest / buildResultManifest. The test never builds a manifest itself.

ONE MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE PLAN. Step 5 says to compare with identityKey (shape:121); my first draft applied identityKey directly to the two raw identities and went red: "expected 'PATH ws/alpha/alpha.txt' to be 'PATH ws\alpha/alpha.txt'". identityKey does NOT normalize - readIdentity (shape:106) does, and admitItems composes readIdentity THEN identityKey. Fixed the test to use the same composition the aggregate uses, so the property is asserted against the production normalizer rather than a convenient one.

Cases (11 generated coverage cases asserted by an exact count):
- happy path over two real files incl. a nested one: identities ws/alpha/alpha.txt and ws/alpha/nested/beta.txt (proves real recursion), byteLength 5 and 4 matching the bytes written, distinct hex64 sha256 facts, sourceProofDigest hex64, exact whole-facts equality, COMPLETE.
- result aspect: a second OPAQUE row workspace-result:ws/alpha with inheritedCount 1 / authoredCount 0, sealed through buildResultManifest against a sealed ScopeObservation.
- DUPLICATE, two arms: the shipped readIdentity folds "ws/alpha" and "ws\alpha" onto one key while the raw spellings differ, and end to end the aggregate answers RECOVERY_INVENTORY_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE + ITEM_REJECTED with 0 items admitted. The enumerator deliberately does not dedupe.
- NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING when nothing was sealed at all; COMPLETE with a hex64 negativeProofDigest when an existing empty root was walked and sealed.
- RESULT_TRUNCATED twice: an unreadable/absent root, and a lister that cannot prove it saw every workspace.
- ENUMERATOR_UNAVAILABLE three ways: lister throws, input manifest refuses to seal (bad baseIdentity), result manifest refuses to seal (authored path out of scope).
- RESULT_OVER_LIMIT at exactly 4097 rows, array length asserted first.

DESIGN NOTE FOR QA - the negative proof is a sealed digest, never a flag. listingComplete:true with zero workspaces produces nothing verifiable, so it is NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING; a root that was walked and sealed empty is COMPLETE because the empty manifest's digest is the artefact that proves someone looked. That is the distinction taskRail 1 asks for.

Per-file counts by grep -c '': workspace-inventory.ts 250, provider-lock-inventory.ts 248 - both at/under the 250 target. .js bridge verified with od -c, trailing LF present. index.ts and index-surface.test.ts untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 4 — prove the registration seam end to end, WITHOUT editing the aggregate (step 1 ruling).

In one of the two test files, compose a registry with createRecoveryInventoryRegistry([providerLockRegistration, workspaceRegistration]) and drive collectRecoveryInventory. Assert:
  - Both classes report COMPLETE only when the enumerator actually proved completeness: items enumerated AND complete:true AND, for an empty result, a non-null negativeProofDigest.
  - Every other case reports UNKNOWN with code RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN at layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER and its specific reason.
  - THE ABSENT-REGISTRATION CASE, which DoD 4 names explicitly: compose a registry OMITTING one of the two classes while it REMAINS in configuredClasses, and assert that class answers UNKNOWN with reason ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED. This is slice 1's "we never looked" invariant — the class must not vanish from the report.
  - Partial items never upgrade a class to COMPLETE, and a later success never launders an earlier UNKNOWN.

Assert coverage proofs by whole-object equality on class, truth, code, reason and layer — not by a .length or truthiness check, so an extra or swapped proof fails.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 4 proven end to end WITHOUT touching the aggregate. Added a "registration seam for both classes" block to workspace-inventory.test.ts that composes createRecoveryInventoryRegistry([providerLockInventoryRegistration(...), workspaceInventoryRegistration(...)]) - exactly the caller-supplied tuple the daemon coordinator will build - and drives collectRecoveryInventory with BOTH classes configured. 17/17 green in the file, typecheck exit 0.

Every arm asserts the WHOLE proof list by deep equality on {class, truth, code, reason, layer} in vocabulary order, not by .length or truthiness, so an extra, missing or swapped proof fails:
- both registered and both provable -> [PROVIDER COMPLETE, WORKSPACE COMPLETE], report coverage COMPLETE, 2 items.
- workspace omitted from the tuple while still in configuredClasses -> [PROVIDER COMPLETE, WORKSPACE UNKNOWN/RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN/ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED/INVENTORY_ADAPTER]. The class does NOT vanish from the report - that is slice 1's "we never looked" invariant.
- the mirror case with the provider omitted, so neither class can pass by being the one that happens to be registered.
- LAUNDERING: provider truncated by an UNOBSERVED process while workspace proves COMPLETE -> coverage UNKNOWN, provider itemCount 0, workspace itemCount 1, and report.items.map(class) === ["WORKSPACE"]. A later COMPLETE cannot lift the earlier UNKNOWN, and the truncated class contributes no partial rows.

COMPLETE is only ever asserted where completeness was actually proven: rows enumerated AND complete:true, or - for the empty workspace arm earlier in the file - a non-null hex64 negativeProofDigest.

The coverage sweep guard moved to the end of the file (vitest runs describes in declaration order, so a sweep declared before these arms would have counted them as zero) and now pins exact hand-written totals: 15 WORKSPACE cases and 4 PROVIDER_PROCESS_LAUNCH_LOCK cases, plus a non-zero overall assertion. Deleting any arm fails the file rather than silently shrinking the sweep.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 5 mutation drills — coverage handling that cannot go red proves nothing. Run each drill, confirm the NAMED case kills it, revert, and confirm green before the next. Record the exact failing assertion for each.

  1. Make the provider enumerator return { status: "ENUMERATED", items: [], complete: true, negativeProofDigest: null } for an empty probe. The NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING case must go RED — this is the "an empty list is not COMPLETE" invariant.
  2. Make a quiet/unobserved process read as terminated. The unobserved-is-not-death case must go RED.
  3. Make the workspace enumerator merge two entries sharing one external identity instead of refusing. The duplicate case must go RED naming RECOVERY_INVENTORY_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE.
  4. Drop one registration from the composed registry. The ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED case must go RED rather than the class silently disappearing from the report.

Back up mutated bytes OUTSIDE the repo and restore with verified sha256 equality.

SHARED-WORKTREE HAZARD: a foreign completion hook can whole-tree commit your mutation while it sits on disk — three such commits landed today (71af97c, a646660, 1e3057a). After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`; a clean diff alone is not proof. Leave no drill residue.

DoD 6 — verification and adversarial review. Run the exact gate LAST, fresh and foreground:

  pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test

Both legs must exit 0 with nonzero discovery. Recorded baseline on this package from the sibling task: 43 files / 1366 tests. Your run must show MORE files — two new test files. A flat file count means your tests never ran.

Path-attributed baseline per project rail: record repo-wide failures at merge-base and at HEAD, require the (HEAD minus merge-base) failing set intersected with owned paths to be EMPTY, and disclose foreign red verbatim with exact lines and paths. Foreign red INSIDE @moe/runner is a BLOCK, not a disclosure — the baseline never excuses package-local red.

Adversarial review before complete_task:
- Did I edit recovery-inventory.ts, index.ts or index-surface.test.ts? I must NOT have. Confirm with `git diff --stat`.

There is nothing there to edit: createRecoveryInventoryRegistry (recovery-inventory.ts:53) takes an immutable caller-supplied tuple, and the function's own doc comment rejects the alternative in terms that name this exact hazard — "a global would be order-dependent, race-prone across concurrent collections, and would let a sibling adapter slice change this aggregate's behaviour by importing it." Slice 2 is precisely that sibling adapter slice. So each module exports a RecoveryInventoryRegistration constant, tests compose their own registry, and the daemon coordinator composes the real one. planningNotes.risks:
1. EDITING THE SLICE-1 AGGREGATE. The description invites it; the design forbids it. A registration edit inside recovery-inventory.ts recreates the module-global coupling slice 1 explicitly refused, and it would collide with slice 3 doing the same. The final diff must show zero changes to that file.

2. TREATING SILENCE AS ABSENCE — the failure this entire class exists to prevent. A quiet process, an empty probe result, or an empty manifest must never read as COMPLETE. Any empty result needs a non-null negativeProofDigest or it is UNKNOWN with NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING.

3. ASSERTING REFUSALS AGAINST A LOCAL HELPER instead of collectRecoveryInventory. The code and layer are minted by the aggregate; a test that checks a private mapping function proves only that the module agrees with itself.
